title: Brigham and Women's Hospital nurses plan strike over contract demands

tea.why: Nurses are protesting for a fair contract, safe patient care, and professional respect, citing an Unfair Labor Practice strike.
tea.want: Nurses want a contract with affordable health insurance, fair compensation, patient care protection, and respect for nurses.
tea.changed: Oct 7: The MNA Bargaining Committee and hospital management agreed to meet on Oct 8 to negotiate and potentially avert the strike.

summary: Nurses at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, represented by the Massachusetts Nurses Association, have scheduled an open-ended strike to begin on October 14, 2026. Approximately 4,000 nurses are seeking a new contract that includes affordable health insurance, fair compensation, protection for patient care, and respect for nurses. The union stated that the strike is an Unfair Labor Practice strike, citing multiple ULP filings against the hospital. Hospital management has expressed readiness to maintain patient care during a strike and is willing to negotiate if the union shows movement on outstanding issues. Both parties are scheduled to meet on October 8 to attempt to avert the strike.
response: The hospital stated it is prepared to provide safe, high-quality care during a strike and remains willing to meet with the MNA "if the union is ready to make meaningful movement toward resolution on the outstanding issues."

updates.text: Brigham nurses, represented by the Massachusetts Nurses Association, provided the hospital with a 10-day strike notice.
The MNA Bargaining Committee and hospital management agreed to meet on October 8 to negotiate a contract.
Hospital management and the MNA Bargaining Committee are scheduled to meet to negotiate a contract and potentially avert the strike.
